prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Atlanta for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the best provider for you depends on the type/complexity of the implant, the provider’s training and experience, and your priorities (cost, location, sedation, timeline). I can help you find a great implant specialist in Atlanta if you tell me your ZIP or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s how to identify the right clinician and some resources to search.

Who to look for
- Type of specialist: for dental implants you’ll commonly see periodontists (gum specialists), oral & maxillofacial surgeons (surgical specialists), and prosthodontists (specialize in crowns/bridges and full-mouth restorations). Complex cases often require a team (surgeon + prosthodontist).
- Training & credentials: look for board certification or diplomate status (AAOMS, ABO/ABOI, American Board of Periodontology), fellowship training, or advanced training in implant dentistry.
- Experience: ask how many implants they place per year and how many similar cases they’ve done (single tooth vs. full-arch, bone grafting/ sinus lifts).

What to ask at a consultation
- Will you get a CBCT 3D scan and a written treatment plan (including timeline and alternatives)?
- Implant system/brand they use and the expected warranty or maintenance plan.
- Who does the restorative crown/bridge — the surgeon or a restorative dentist/prosthodontist?
- Complication and success rates for similar cases; examples and before/after photos.
- Whether bone grafts/sinus lifts are expected and what that adds to time/cost.
- Sedation options and post-op care.
- Total cost breakdown (implant, abutment, crown, grafts, additional visits).

Technology and practice features to prefer
- CBCT and 3D planning (guided surgery)
- In-house lab work or a prosthodontist partner for predictable esthetics
- Clear pre/post-op protocols and follow-up care
- Good patient reviews/testimonials and photos of past cases

Where to search and verify providers
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) find-a-dentist
- American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) directory
- American College of Prosthodontists / American Academy of Periodontology directories
- Local hospital/academic centers (Emory’s dental/oral surgery clinics)
- Patient review sites: Google, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Yelp (look for patterns, not single reviews)

If you want, I can:
- Find highly rated implant specialists in Atlanta if you give your ZIP or neighborhood and tell me whether you need a single implant, multiple, or full-arch and whether budget/insurance is important.
